name: Ikobi
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.note: Only Ikobi-Mena Swadesh lists located (archive.org/rosettaproject); no phonology/grammar found

tone_statements.citation: Usher, Timothy. 2020-2024. Omati River (Papuan Gulf > Kikori River > Rumu-Omati River). New Guinea World: An online catalogue and classification of the languages of New Guinea. Santa Fe Institute / hosted by Universitat Zurich (newguineaworld.linguistik.uzh.ch); page last modified 2024-06-25.
tone_statements.quote: Nasalization is contrastive, but is difficult to reconstruct because it is preserved only sporadically in Kaser. ... Tone is contrastive, but has not been indicated in the protoforms below.
tone_statements.locator: HTML page, section 'Historical phonology' (after the proto-vowel and diphthong inventory, before 'Initial consonants correspond as follows')
tone_statements.summary: Tone stated to be contrastive for the Omati River languages (Kaser = Ikobi, Mouwase, Barikewa); number/type of tones, tone-bearing unit and processes not stated; Petterson's phonemic Kaser transcriptions show at least high (acute), low (grave), and macron/circumflex-marked syllables; nothing on stress apart from one remark that a vowel is 'destressed in a compound' in Mouwase.

sources.citation: Bullock, Juliann. 2015. The Sociolinguistic Situation in the Kaser Area. SIL Electronic Survey Report 2015-001. Dallas: SIL International. 73 pp.
sources.note: Nothing on word stress. Appendix A 'Language characteristics' (printed p.34) states negation in Ikobi (and Mouwase, Barikewa) 'can be indicated tonally' with the pair kàrímào 'he is sitting' / kárímào 'he is not sitting'; wordlists in App. C carry pitch diacritics but no stress marks or prosodic commentary.

sources.citation: Wurm, S.A. 1975. Eastern Central Trans-New Guinea Phylum languages. In S.A. Wurm (ed.), New Guinea area languages and language study, vol. 1. Pacific Linguistics C-38: 461-526.
sources.note: 2.7.6.5 (pp.507-509) 'Comparatively little is known of the structure of these languages'; brief phonology notes are for KAIRI (Rumu) only: 'Suprasegmentals: No reliable information is available but the materials suggest the presence of a two-tone system with low functional load.' (p.508). Nothing on Ikobi/Mena suprasegmentals.
